t: A merchant city-state of the Russian north that elected its officials and archbishop and hired princes by contract.
It ruled a huge fur-producing hinterland to the White Sea and the Urals and traded with the Hanseatic League.
Ivan III of Moscow crushed its army in 1471, annexed it in 1478 and took away its veche bell.
dyk: Archaeologists have found over a thousand birchbark letters in Novgorod, including a thirteenth-century boy Onfim’s school exercises and drawings.
ev: Novgorodians expel Prince Vsevolod Mstislavich; the republic begins
Novgorod repels the army of Andrey Bogolyubsky
Alexander Nevsky defeats the Livonian knights on Lake Peipus
Treaty of Nöteborg draws the first border with Sweden
Treaty of Bolotovo recognises Pskov’s independence
Treaty of Yazhelbitsy limits Novgorod’s independence
Ivan III’s army defeats Novgorod at the Shelon River
Novgorod surrenders to Ivan III; the veche bell is taken to Moscow

f.founder: Citizens of Novgorod (expulsion of Vsevolod Mstislavich, 1136)
